components.css: .ds-activity-strip{font-family:'Manrope Variable','Segoe UI',sans-serif;margin-top:24px;min-width:0;color:var(--ink, #27382f);background:transparent;}.ds-gpu-name{margin:0 0 12px;color:var(--muted, #657069);font-size:12px;font-weight:650;line-height:1.5;overflow-wrap:anywhere;}.ds-hour-track{position:relative;}.ds-hour-columns{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(25,minmax(0,1fr));gap:5px;}.ds-hour{box-sizing:border-box;display:block;min-width:0;height:32px;padding:0;border-radius:4px;background:#e8ede4;border:1px solid #75896f;cursor:pointer;transition:background-color 140ms ease-out,border-color 140ms ease-out;}.ds-hour-active{background:#42684c;border-color:#42684c;}.ds-hour-selected,.ds-hour:hover,.ds-hour:focus-visible{background:#d2dfc3;border-color:var(--green, #3d6548);}.ds-hour-active.ds-hour-selected,.ds-hour-active:hover,.ds-hour-active:focus-visible{background:#284e36;border-color:#284e36;}.ds-hour:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--green, #3d6548);outline-offset:3px;}.ds-activity-old .ds-hour{background:#e8ede4;}.ds-activity-old .ds-hour-active{background:#74876d;border-color:#74876d;}.ds-hour-tooltip{position:absolute;bottom:calc(100% + 10px);left:clamp(76px,var(--position),calc(100% - 76px));transform:translateX(-50%);z-index:2;padding:9px 12px;border-radius:7px;background:var(--ink, #27382f);color:var(--surface, #f7f8f5);box-shadow:0 4px 12px rgb(24 45 31 / .14);font-size:12px;line-height:1.5;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums;white-space:nowrap;pointer-events:none;}.ds-hour-tooltip strong{font-weight:750;}.ds-sr-only{position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;padding:0;margin:-1px;overflow:hidden;clip:rect(0,0,0,0);white-space:nowrap;border:0;}@media(max-width:480px){.ds-hour-columns{gap:3px;}.ds-hour{height:30px;border-radius:3px;}}@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-hour{transition:none;}}

narrative.overview:
Shambu is a quiet status instrument for a personal GPU server. The readiness sentence, external connection address, and four aligned readings establish the hierarchy. Chalk surfaces, green ink, and fine rules keep the interface light. A narrow GPU history strip follows the readings at the same width.

The native R2-D2 app icon carries the character of the product. The dashboard begins directly with the readiness message and Connection control. Its personality comes from concise language, careful spacing, and the simple rhythm of hourly activity columns.
keyCharacteristics: A light interface with one continuous column.
A readiness header, external endpoint strip, and four aligned status rows.
Visible recovery guidance and a model-library disclosure grounded in actual data.
A narrow rolling 24-hour GPU strip with local-time hover and focus details.
Native identity without a repeated dashboard wordmark or portrait.

rules.name: The Evidence Color Rule
rules.body: Use green for a confirmed positive readiness state, amber for attention, and rust for an error. Unknown, idle, and stale readiness states use the muted neutral. Pair each reading with words and a drawn state mark.

rules.name: The Binary Hour Rule
rules.body: An activity column has two visual states, Active or Idle. A filled hour represents a qualifying observed GPU sample while an Ollama model was in GPU memory. Empty and unmonitored hours display Idle.

rules.name: The Single Typeface Rule
rules.body: Use Manrope throughout the interface. Distinguish readings, controls, and explanations through size and weight, with tabular figures for times and model sizes.

rules.name: The Flat Surface Rule
rules.body: Separate persistent surfaces with spacing, a fine border, or a tonal fill. Reserve the small soft shadow for the temporary hour tooltip.

dos: Do use the implemented palette and self-hosted Manrope.
Do lead with the readiness sentence and external connection address.
Do use Active consistently for healthy service checks.
Do keep failure details visible and reserve model expansion for actual installed models.
Do place the GPU name above a full-width 24-hour strip with accessible hour descriptions and hover or focus details.
Do preserve keyboard focus, accessible control names, and reduced-motion behavior.
Do keep character artwork in the native app identity.
Do use generic examples and keep personal connection details out of public artifacts.
donts: Don't add a duplicate wordmark, portrait, or decorative hero above the dashboard.
Don't give ordinary status rows empty disclosures or hide recovery guidance behind a click.
Don't turn the readiness list into a grid of separate cards.
Don't describe the binary history as request counts or exact inference attribution.
Don't use color alone to communicate a reading.
Don't add shadows to persistent containers, glass, textures, or decorative data imagery.
Don't use em dashes in product copy or public documentation.
